comments.content: Directory classification can allow HEAD moves in the protected repository after ordinary relative navigation. For a root of /work/repo, `cd /work && cd repo && git reset --hard` leaves `inside=0`, even though Git runs in /work/repo. Likewise, `git -C /tmp/../work/repo reset --hard` is classified as external. Track the effective working directory and normalize relative paths and `..` components before comparing it with the project root.

Common Git global options bypass this check entirely: `git --no-pager reset --hard` and `git -c advice.detachedHead=false checkout HEAD~1` do not match, so both are allowed in the protected worktree. Parse supported global options before identifying the subcommand, including their argument values and any `-C` directory changes.

Quoted directory paths are truncated at the first space. If the project root is `/work/my project`, `cd "/work/my project" && git reset --hard` passes `/work/my` to `outside()`, marks the command as external, and allows the reset. The `git -C` matcher also fails to recognize a quoted path containing spaces. Preserve complete quoted path arguments when parsing both forms so projects in directories containing spaces remain protected.

Shell redirections and comments are counted as positional Git arguments, so an ordinary revision reset such as `git reset HEAD~1 >/dev/null` (or `git reset HEAD~1 # undo`) has more than one entry in `pos` and is allowed. Both commands move HEAD in the protected worktree, and the existing write checks permit `/dev/null`. Exclude shell redirections and comments before counting Git arguments.

The opening subshell parenthesis is removed, but the closing one remains in the arguments. Consequently, `(git reset --hard)` is parsed with `--hard)` rather than `--hard`; it matches neither the mode check nor the positional-revision check and is allowed to reset the protected worktree. Handle closing shell grouping delimiters as well as opening ones before classifying reset arguments.
